Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mean verb

intend

also intend, mean to, on purpose, I didn’t mean to, what do you mean?, propose to do

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.11: nōbīs erat in animō Cicerōnem ad Caesarem mittere
Liv. praef. 6: ea nec adfirmāre nec refellere in animō est
Traupman 104: in animō habēre (+ inf.)

in animō habēre

mean to, intend (with an infinitive)

Also mihi in animō est, with an infinitive.

Examples

  • ea nec adfirmāre nec refellere in animō est

    I don’t mean either to vouch for these stories or to refute them.Liv. praef. 6

  • Hic respondēre voluit, nōn lacessere.

    He meant to answer, not to provoke.Ter. Ph. 19

  • Quid tu tibi vīs?

    What do you mean by it?Ter. Eun. 797

  • Nōn cōnsultō fēcī, tata.

    I didn’t mean to, Daddy.composed

Other words

  • volō, velle, voluī — mean to, intend

    verb, irregular · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 19: Hic respondēre voluit, nōn lacessere.; Ter. Eun. 797: Quid tu tibi vīs?

    Lewis & Short: “to intend, purpose, mean”. “I meant to” is often simply volēbam; Quid tibi vīs?, “What do you mean (by this)? What are you after?”.

  • cōgitō, cōgitāre, cōgitāvī, cōgitātum — intend, plan (with an infinitive)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cato, Agr. 1.1: praedium quom parāre cōgitābis

    Lewis & Short: “to have something in mind, to intend, meditate, design, plan”.

  • cōnsultō — on purpose

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.27: an cōnsultō et cōgitātā fīat injūria

    Nōn cōnsultō fēcī: I didn’t mean to.

  • imprūdēns, imprūdentis — without meaning to, unawares

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 880: fēcī imprūdēns quam sciēns; Traupman 104: by mistake, imprūdēns

    Agrees with the subject: imprūdēns fēcī, I did it without meaning to.

See also mean, want, think, really?.
